project.title: AI PhD & Research Roles
project.purpose: getting into an AI PhD or AI research role
project.objective: Get the user into an AI PhD or research role, through to interviews.
project.flow: discover → analyse → contact → prepare → submit → interview

folders.name: 01_profile
folders.holds: The user's details and documents, as imported by the user

folders.name: 02_research
folders.holds: General knowledge about getting in, independent of any one opportunity; research-brief.md and evidence-log.md

folders.name: 03_discovery
folders.holds: sources.md (where we search) and searches/ (a dated log of each search sweep)

folders.name: 04_entities
folders.holds: Reusable dossiers: institutions/, programs/, people/, funders/

folders.name: 05_materials
folders.holds: Master materials: CV, statements, proposals, answer bank, referees, writing samples

folders.name: 06_outreach
folders.holds: Message templates, outreach-log.csv and networking/ (contact not tied to one opportunity)

folders.name: 07_opportunities
folders.holds: One folder per shortlisted opportunity, holding everything specific to it

folders.name: 08_interviews
folders.holds: General interview prep (one interview's prep goes in its opportunity folder)

folders.name: 09_admin
folders.holds: Language tests, degree recognition, visas, fees, portal accounts (no passwords)

filing_rule: Decision rule: *is it about one opportunity?* → its `07_opportunities/` folder. *Is it reusable?* → `04_entities/` (a who or what), `05_materials/` (something we send) or `02_research/` (something we learned).

tracker.name: pipeline

card_sections.heading: Summary
card_sections.hint: One paragraph: what the position is, who funds it, why it is (or isn't) a fit.

card_sections.heading: Key facts
card_sections.hint: Deadline, required documents, eligibility gates, contract or stipend, start date. Official sources only; cite the file in sources/ or the URL.

card_sections.heading: Analysis
card_sections.hint: Criteria verbatim from the advert; evidence against each from 01_profile/; red flags; angle; verdict and fit 1-5.

tracker.notes: `ready` means filled in and handed back for the user to submit. The user always presses submit.

agents.name: research-lead
agents.description: Head of Research. Use for deep research on how to get into AI PhDs and research roles: selection criteria, country systems, funding and eligibility, base rates, field strategy.
agents.mission: Your job is evidence the team can act on, not volume.
agents.jobs: Deep research on admissions, countries, funding, base rates; keeps evidence-log.md
standards: Anything that drives an action (a date, an eligibility rule, a required document) needs a primary source. Record it in `02_research/evidence-log.md` with the URL and date checked.
Secondary sources (surveys, guides, forums) can raise hypotheses. Say so when that is all you have.
agents.memory_focus: which sources are reliable or blocked, search strategies that worked

agents.name: opportunity-scout
agents.description: Head of Discovery. Use to sweep sources for new PhD positions, research roles, fellowships and internships, log every search, and add leads to the tracker.
agents.mission: You find opportunities early and log every search so nothing is swept twice.
agents.jobs: Sweeps sources, logs every search, adds leads
steps: Log each sweep in `03_discovery/searches/YYYY-MM-DD_<source>.md`: queries, filters, hits, what was added.
standards: Add leads only with `tools/tracker.py add`; never promote or change status.
agents.memory_focus: which job boards and lab pages are productive, query patterns that work

agents.name: intel-analyst
agents.description: Head of Intelligence. Use for dossiers on institutions, programmes, supervisors and funders, and for fit analysis and go/no-go recommendations on shortlisted opportunities.
agents.mission: You turn a lead into a decision: who they are, what they want, and whether the user fits.

agents.name: outreach-lead
agents.description: Head of Communications and Positioning. Use for the user's narrative and for drafting cold emails, follow-ups and referee requests (drafts only).
agents.mission: You write messages a busy academic will actually read and answer.
agents.jobs: Positioning; cold emails, follow-ups, referee requests (drafts only)

agents.name: materials-writer
agents.description: Head of Application Content. Use for CVs, statements, research proposals, the answer bank, and tailoring them to one opportunity.
agents.mission: You write application documents that are true, specific and tailored.
agents.jobs: CV, statements, proposals, answer bank, tailoring
standards: Every claim about the user traces to a file in `01_profile/`. A missing fact is reported, never invented.

agents.name: operations-lead
agents.description: Chief of Operations. Use for application logistics: portal forms up to the final review page (never submitting), deadlines, required documents, tests, fees, accounts, tracker status updates.
agents.mission: You make sure nothing is missed, late or wrong on a form.
agents.jobs: Portals and forms up to ready (never submits), deadlines, documents, fees
never: Never click a final submit button, pay a fee or tick a consent box the brief doesn't authorise.

agents.name: interview-coach
agents.description: Interview Coach. Use for interview preparation, mock questions and debriefs.
agents.mission: You get the user ready for the conversation that decides the outcome.

checks: **Fit to the opportunity:** every essential criterion in the advert is addressed or the gap is declared.

writing.kinds: emails, messages, statements, CVs, proposals and form answers
writing.recipients: a busy supervisor, an admissions committee, a recruiter
writing.concrete: named methods, datasets, results with baselines, dates, places

sources.scope: research, discovery, dossiers, fit analysis, admin facts, interview prep, and facts about a recipient in outreach

tiers.T1: The institution, programme, funder or government in its own words (official pages, calls, regulations, handbooks); the supervisor's own lab or university page; peer-reviewed papers and their official venue pages; official statistics
tiers.T2: Established job boards and portals that republish adverts (they link back to the original), recognised professional bodies, established news outlets, university-run guidance, well-cited preprints
tiers.T3: Forums (Reddit, GradCafe, Quora), personal blogs, Medium or Substack posts, social media, video, wikis, SEO listicles, content farms

waiting_on_user: Import their details and documents into `01_profile/`.
Decide the scope: countries, intake year, fields, funded-only or not (record in `00_hub/decisions.md`).
Agree the research brief: which questions, in what order (`02_research/research-brief.md`).
first_steps: CoS: agree the research brief with the user, then split it into tasks for `research-lead`.
CoS: set up `03_discovery/sources.md` with the user, then brief `opportunity-scout` for a first sweep.
CoS: promote the strongest leads, then brief `intel-analyst` for deep dives.
